Hi Emily — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

• Recap: you want an inference solution for your document ingestion and summarization workflows (PHI in some pipelines), ~4 steady TPS with spikes to 12 TPS, and aggressive latency targets for real-time UI (~200–300ms tail for short prompts).
• Primary constraint: data residency / PHI — you mentioned VPC or on-prem are possibilities, but your team is open to starting on Dedicated capacity if network segregation and encryption at rest meet compliance.

As we discussed, we need a few concrete data points to size Dedicated accurately:
1) Traffic profile: steady vs peak TPS, typical session concurrency, daily/weekly patterns.
2) Token mix: average prompt tokens, average completion tokens, 95th percentile length.
3) Model preference / openness to quantized variants (e.g., FP16 H100 vs int8 on A100-style stacks).
4) Any hard latency SLOs for first-byte and end-to-end UI timings.

Can you confirm the items below (short bullets or a sample trace is fine):
- Typical steady TPS: ?
- Worst-case peak TPS sustained for >1 minute: ?
- Avg prompt tokens / avg completion tokens: ?
- Concurrency target (simultaneous in-flight requests): ?
- Requirement for private VPC vs dedicated with VPC peering / dedicated-only: ?

I've looped in Karthik (solutions) and Priyom (sales ops) on this thread to start mapping options and a sizing worksheet. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30–45 minute sizing workshop next week and share our capacity worksheet in advance.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Emily — share short traffic snapshot or answers to the bullets above by EOD Tue 6/22.
2) Redwood — Karthik will propose two initial Dedicated configurations (GPU family tradeoffs + estimated concurrency headroom).
3) If alignment — we run a short on-site/remote benchmark with a small test corpus before formal sizing commitment.

Attachments: I will send our capacity worksheet when Karthik populates the initial numbers (placeholder attached soon).

Thanks Rishi — great summary. Answers inline below and a couple clarifications:

- Typical steady TPS: ~4 TPS across our primary region (US-west).
- Worst-case peak TPS (sustained ~2–3 minutes): 12 TPS (we see bursts when large cohorts run batch ingestion).
- Avg prompt tokens: 120 tokens. Avg completion tokens: 350 tokens. 95th percentile completion: ~900 tokens.
- Concurrency target: we expect ~6–10 simultaneous user sessions during peak; if you plan per-request concurrency we expect ~8 in-flight requests as a target.
- Private VPC: required for PHI workflows; for non-PHI we could start on Dedicated with peering but legally we need to run PHI pipelines only within a private VPC or on-prem. Our plan = start non-PHI on Dedicated, migrate PHI to VPC when ready.

Additional notes:
- Model: open to 70B-class Llama-family variants. We need guidance on quantized performance tradeoffs; cost is a factor but not at the expense of latency doubling.
- Security: SOC 2 plus KMS integration required before PHI migration.

Thanks — added a draft worksheet and quick notes (attached). High-level comments up-front:

1) GPU family tradeoffs:
- A100-int8 config (cost-optimized): expect ~300–450ms median for 70B quantized int8 depending on tokenization pattern; throughput per GPU ~40–60 tokens/sec steady for mixed-length requests; good cost/TPS but tail latency can spike with large completions (p95 closer to 1s without batching control).
- H100-fp16 config (latency-optimized): expect ~180–300ms median, better p95 (400–550ms) and significantly higher throughput when using optimized kernels; higher cost per GPU but fewer nodes needed for given TPS.

2) Concurrency and KV cache:
- For multi-turn sessions we recommend sticky routing to keep KV caches warm on the same worker. That reduces repeated KV population overhead and improves tail latency for conversational flows. Expect 15–25% latency benefit for hot sessions.

3) Batching guidance:
- Use small, latency-aware batching windows (5–10ms) for UI traffic. For batch ingestion (non-interactive) run separate pool with larger batch windows to maximize throughput. Separate pools simplifies autoscale policy.

4) Autoscaling buffers: 40% headroom at steady-state to absorb short bursts; configure fast scale-up (30s) and slower scale-down (5–10m) to avoid thrash.

I've attached: cleverdata_capacity_worksheet_v1.xlsx (populated with initial assumptions) and sample_traffic_trace_202605.json (normalized). Next steps:
- Emily / CleverData: confirm whether PHI migration date is within next 60 days (affects VPC onboarding priority).
- Redwood: propose a 45-minute sizing workshop to walk through the worksheet and validate assumptions with Emily's infra/ML eng leads.
